fields.description: What Atlas boots the machine from. install.sh expects a Debian or Ubuntu image: it installs with apt.
fields.label: Base Image

fields.description: The VM datum runs on, built by Atlas. Set when the node is requested.
fields.label: Machine

fields.description:
Draft — no machine yet, or it is still booting.
Setting Up — installing datum on the machine.
Active — datum is running and answering.
Failed — the machine died, or the last install did not finish. See the Setup Log.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: DATUM_REPOSITORY. Cloned onto the host at install.
fields.label: Repository

fields.description: DATUM_VERSION. A branch, tag or commit. A branch follows origin on every install; a commit is pinned.
fields.label: Version

fields.description: Where ClickHouse is, and the admin password the migration needs. The `datum` and `insights` users are created by the migration; their passwords are generated here.
fields.label: ClickHouse

fields.description: DATUM_CLICKHOUSE_HOST. The install puts ClickHouse on this machine, so it answers on loopback.
fields.label: Host

fields.description: The `default` superuser, set by the install. Only the migration uses it, to create the other two users.
fields.label: Default User Password

fields.description: The `datum` user, which the API writes as. Generated here and created by the migration.
fields.label: Datum User Password

fields.description: The `insights` user, which Insights reads ClickHouse with directly. Datum never uses it.
fields.label: Insights User Password

fields.description: Was this datum server auto spawned?
fields.label: Auto Spawn

fields.description: Setup runs Cargo started by itself. It stops trying once the budget is spent.
fields.label: Auto Setup Attempts
